text.p: Biscuit maker Arnotts Ltd said on Thursday it was confident of improved performance in 1996/97.

"As for the outlook for Arnotts this year, I am confident that the direction that we have set is correct and that the strategies in place will improve the company's performance," said Arnotts managing director Chris Roberts told the company's annual general meeting.
Arnotts is about 70 percent owned by Campbell Soup Co.
Roberts said Arnotts had taken a number of initiatives to revitalise the business and generate volume growth.
The company had increased expenditure on product development and marketing support and recently introduced the SnackRight biscuit range.
Arnotts had also purchased the Kettle Chip company and planned to grow this to a successful national brand.
Roberts said Arnotts had also implemented a programme to review its resources, processes, and structures which was expected to lead to annual savings of about A$16 million by 1998.
Arnotts increased net profit by 7.7 percent to A$60.9 million in the 13 months to July 28, 1996.
The result included an abnormal loss of A$13.0 million linked to the relocation of a Sydney factory.
Arnotts shares opened steady at A$8.45 on Thursday.
